html:
The Non-Aligned Movement was founded at a summit in Belgrade in September 1961, bringing together states that refused to join either the American or the Soviet bloc in the Cold War.

Its leaders were Tito of Yugoslavia, Nehru of India, Nasser of Egypt, Sukarno of Indonesia and Nkrumah of Ghana, building on the Bandung conference of 1955. Twenty five countries attended the first summit; most of the newly independent states of Asia and Africa joined later. The movement called for an end to colonialism and for peaceful coexistence, though its members often leaned one way or the other. For Yugoslavia, after the split with Stalin, it was a way to matter in the world without choosing a side.
sum: The Non-Aligned Movement was founded at a summit in Belgrade in September 1961, bringing together states that refused to join either the American or the Soviet bloc in the Cold War.
